definitions.explanation: A reckless or foolish act committed because of the impulsiveness and inexperience of youth.

examples.japanese: ⟦あれ→あれ：00916_are⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りだった。
{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{中退|ちゅうたい}→中退：11355_chuutai⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧しまった。
examples.english: In the folly of youth, I dropped out of college.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧になって⟦{思|おも}えば→思う：00492_omou⟧、⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧{時|とき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{行動|こうどう}→行動：02728_koudou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りだった⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{反省|はんせい}している→反省する：21398_hanseisuru⟧。
examples.english: Looking back now, I regret that what I did back then was the folly of youth.

notes:
An idiomatic expression used to look back on past mistakes with a sense of self-deprecation or wry acceptance. It implies that the mistake was driven by youthful energy, overconfidence, or naivety rather than malice.

The word ⟦{若気|わかげ}→若気：17795_wakage⟧ refers to youthful spirit or impulsiveness, and {至|いた}り means "the height of" or "the extreme of," so the expression literally means "the extreme of youthful spirit."

USAGE:
Almost always used retrospectively — the speaker has matured and is reflecting on a past action. It carries a tone of mild embarrassment rather than deep regret. Often preceded by ⟦あれ→あれ：00916_are⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ or followed by だった.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りだった: it was a youthful indiscretion
- {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りで〜⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧しまった: ended up doing ~ out of youthful folly
- {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}えば→言う：00515_iu⟧{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り: if you call it youthful folly, that's what it was

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {血気|けっき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧はやる: to be hot-blooded and impulsive (describes the state, not a past reflection)
- ⟦{後悔|こうかい}→後悔：02738_koukai⟧: regret (more general and serious in tone)
